newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican drought to raise soybean imports -industry.
newsitem.headline: Mexican drought to raise soybean imports -industry.

text.p: Drought-stricken Mexico will have to increase soybean imports to 2.6 million tonnes after what will be its worst harvest in history, an industry spokesman told Reuters on Monday.
"Mexico's soybean production will be at an all-time low," said Gonzalo Cardenas Jimenez, presidente of the Western Edible Oil Chamber, referring to the 12-month crop cycle begining October 1996.
Cardenas said that the drought currently afflicting a large part of Mexico would force an approximately 400,000-tonne increase in imports of soybeans, used to produce edible oils and fats.
Projected imports for the 1996-97 cycle compare with an expected total of 2.23 million tonnes by the close of the 1995/96 cycle in October.

Mexico imports 95 percent of its soybeans from the United States and most of the rest comes from Brazil, said Cardenas, whose chamber members account for 66 percent of all edible oils and fats produced in Mexico.
Cardenas expected soybean production to fall to 50,000 tonnes this calendar year, compared to 135,000 tons in 1995.
